start.title: Start making better apps
start.meta.description: Tell your coding agent what you want to make and try the app it builds at a public link for 24 hours. No account or install needed.
start.intro: One line for your agent which will get you up and running with the CARLOS tools to build and deploy a small app with its own database.
start.steps: Paste the line and say what you want to make.
Answer a few questions about how it should look and feel. If asked, allow it to connect to one website.
Open the link your agent gives you.
start.lifetime: Your demo is public for 24 hours from when it is made. Anyone with the link can open it. Updates do not extend the 24 hours.
start.data: Nothing is backed up. Use made-up data. Do not enter real passwords or personal information.
start.terms_line: Demos follow our demo terms, and anyone can report one that breaks them.
start.claim: If you like it, enter your email address and the code we send. The app moves to a permanent address in a new or existing account. If you have more than one account, choose where it goes.
start.account: For a larger project or an app you already have, use an account.

home.replay.title: Your agent
home.replay.status-page.agent.1: I’ve read the directions. They ask me to check a few things with you before I build anything, so here are the questions.
home.replay.status-page.q1: What would you like to make?
home.replay.status-page.you.2: I run operations at Ledgerlight, a small invoicing software company. We need a public status page. … Only our staff should be able to post incidents and updates; a shared staff passphrase is fine for now. … It should feel calm and trustworthy, like a proper status page. I’m not technical, so keep it simple for me.
home.replay.status-page.plan: Here’s what I plan to build. … The look: calm and trustworthy. Off-white page, dark navy text, one muted teal for the brand, and clear status colours that always have a word next to them. …
home.replay.status-page.p2: Everything works: posting needs the passphrase, and resolving an incident sets the part back to Working. …
home.replay.status-page.p3: The phone layout passes: nothing scrolls sideways and every button and field is at least 44 px tall. …
home.replay.status-page.p4: Your Ledgerlight status page is live:
home.replay.status-page.shot.alt: The live status page: Ledgerlight’s “Some systems are slow: API” banner, its four parts marked Working or Slow, and an ongoing incident.
home.replay.defect-log.agent.1: I’ve read the CARLOS start directions. They say to ask you a few questions before building anything, so here they are:
home.replay.defect-log.q1: What would you like to make?
home.replay.defect-log.q2: How should it look and feel?
home.replay.defect-log.q3: How much detail do you want from me?
home.replay.defect-log.you.2: I’m the quality manager at Corrin Mouldings, a small plastics manufacturer with three production lines (Line 1, Line 2, Line 3). I’d like a defect log … Show the recent defects, plus counts by line and by type for the last 7 days, with a simple chart. It should feel industrial and data-first. I’m not technical, so keep it simple for me.
home.replay.defect-log.plan: Before I write anything, here’s the plan in plain terms: … Look: plain and industrial. It’ll have a dark steel-grey header with the company name and a small logo mark, a light grey page and one safety-orange accent. …
home.replay.defect-log.p1: Now writing the app: the Go server, the page template and the styling.
home.replay.defect-log.p4: Your defect log is live and loads correctly:
home.replay.defect-log.shot.alt: The live defect log: a dark Corrin Mouldings header, a “Log a defect” form with line, defect type and quantity, and the last 7 days’ totals.
home.replay.project-board.agent.1: I’ve read the directions on that page. … Step one is to ask you a few questions and wait for your answers before I build anything.
home.replay.project-board.q1: What do you want to make?
home.replay.project-board.q3: What’s the one main screen, and what does it save?
home.replay.project-board.you.2: I’m the studio manager at Okafor Lind Architects, a small practice. I’d like a project status board for our current projects. … The board shows projects grouped by stage, with anything late or at risk easy to spot. It should feel refined and minimal, like an architecture studio. I’m not technical, so keep it simple for me.
home.replay.project-board.plan: Your design is a good fit for this. … The look: quiet and refined, like a studio drawing board. It uses warm off-white paper, charcoal text, a single muted terracotta accent and serif headings …
home.replay.project-board.p1: I’ve confirmed the starter is intact, so now I’m writing the app … the board page and its styling.
home.replay.project-board.p3: The page looks right on both phone and desktop. …
home.replay.project-board.p4: Your project board is live and working:
home.replay.project-board.shot.alt: The live project board: Okafor Lind Architects’ counts of active, at-risk and late projects, then project cards grouped by stage, marked On track or At risk.
home.replay.band-gigs.agent.1: I’ve read the CARLOS directions. … Before I write any code, the directions say I need a few answers from you:
home.replay.band-gigs.q1: What do you want to make?
home.replay.band-gigs.q2: How should it look and feel?
home.replay.band-gigs.q3: What’s the one main screen, and what’s the one kind of thing it saves?
home.replay.band-gigs.you.2: I’m in a small band called The Marrow Lights. I’d like a page with our upcoming gigs and a mailing-list sign-up, so people leave their name and email to hear about new shows. … Put a line on it like “Loud songs for quiet towns.” I want it to feel moody, like an old gig poster on a wall. …
home.replay.band-gigs.plan: Before I build it, here’s my plan. … Like a gig poster pasted on a dark wall: near-black background, aged off-white paper panels, one strong rust-red accent … and a faint grain pattern behind everything.
home.replay.band-gigs.p1: … Now I’m writing the app: the poster page, the sign-up form, and the private sign-ups page.
home.replay.band-gigs.p2: On phones, “MARROW” splits across two lines because of the fallback font, so I’ll make the band name a bit smaller on small screens.
home.replay.band-gigs.p3: The page looks right on phones too. …
home.replay.band-gigs.p4: Your band page is built and online. You can open it here:
home.replay.band-gigs.shot.alt: The live band page: a torn gig poster for The Marrow Lights with “Loud songs for quiet towns.” and the upcoming gigs as taped-up strips.
home.replay.climbing-gym.agent.1: I’ve read the CARLOS getting-started directions. The first step is to ask you a few things before I build anything.
home.replay.climbing-gym.you.2: I run a small climbing gym called Granite Yard. I’d like a route board page … Save the sends and show who’s sent what, with the most-sent routes up top. … I want it to feel bold and energetic, like a gym wall with loud colours. …
home.replay.climbing-gym.plan: Here’s what I’m planning. … The look: a dark, chalky charcoal wall with bright, chunky route cards in your hold colours, a punchy yellow “Log send” button … so it feels like walking into the gym.
home.replay.climbing-gym.p1: Starter verified and extracted. Now writing the app.
home.replay.climbing-gym.p2: The app works locally: sends save, the most-sent route moves to the top, and bad input is rejected. …
home.replay.climbing-gym.p4: Your Granite Yard Route Board is live:
home.replay.climbing-gym.shot.alt: The live route board: a loud yellow Granite Yard header, a count of sends logged, and a “Log a send” form on a dark wall.

home.what.heading: CARLOS is a system for building better quality, more resilient, secure web apps that deploy easily.
home.what.sub: Inspired by UNIX principles, CARLOS deploys full stack web apps as single processes rather than sprawling containerised services, using fast compiled languages. This unlocks a slew of benefits.
home.what.follow: It’s defined by an open specification.
home.what.props.title: A typical CARLOS app is
home.what.prop1.title: One file
home.what.prop1.body: Web server, database engine, background jobs and interface, compiled into a single binary.
home.what.prop2.title: A database per customer
home.what.prop2.body: Every customer gets their own instance and their own data. Nothing shared, nothing to leak across.
home.what.prop3.title: Asleep until needed
home.what.prop3.body: It stops when nobody is using it and wakes on the next request, with nothing lost.
home.what.prop4.title: At home anywhere
home.what.prop4.body: The same binary runs on a hosted platform, your own servers or a laptop.
home.what.prop5.title: For people and agents
home.what.prop5.body: What a person can do in the interface, an agent can do through the API or the command line.
home.practice.lead: Best practices built in, by default
home.practice.1.name: Performance
home.practice.2.name: Security
home.practice.3.name: Accessibility
home.practice.4.name: Privacy

home.tools.heading: To make it easy, we built an agent-first modern web framework to build apps and a platform to deploy them on
home.tools.rastrillo.body: A full-stack Go web framework. Ready-made parts, so your agent writes less from scratch.
home.tools.platform.body: Get your CARLOS apps online with HTTPS, backups, provisioning, observability and analytics. Static sites work great too.
home.tools.skill.body: The CARLOS skill has everything it needs to build and deploy a sample app and get it live right now.
